subject: Ops constraints, ramp timeline, and tenant segmentation plan - follow-up (Helixa)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@helixa.ai>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@helixa.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Ops constraints, ramp timeline, and tenant segmentation plan - follow-up (Helixa)

Hi Samira / Jordan —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick post‑call synthesis and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we put numbers into the worksheet.

Key pain points you called out
- Predictable latency for interactive inference during clinical demo windows (spikes today cause 300–800ms jitter).
- Regulatory requirement to keep PHI workloads logically isolated with strict audit logs.
- Need an obvious procurement path with a short pilot and predictable cost ramp.

Success criteria we agreed on
- p95 generation latency <= 250ms for 256‑token responses under normal load; p95 <= 450ms during 2x demo peaks.
- Tenant isolation with per-tenant KMS and auditable request logs retained 90+ days.
- Demonstrable 30% reduction in per‑token cost after caching/quantization guidance in the pilot period.

Redwood proposal (summary)
- Reserved baseline: 4 dedicated slots (N GPUs per slot depending on model selection) to guarantee isolation and steady throughput.
- Burst strategy: automated bump to shared burst pool for infrequent peaks (policy-based routing, auto‑fallback to smaller quantized model if capacity constrained).
- SLA targets: 99.95% availability for the dedicated pool; configurable latency SLOs with tracing hooks for incident analysis.

Immediate asks / next steps
- We’ll upload a filled capacity worksheet (attached) with two scenarios (base + burst) for your review by EOD tomorrow — owner: Ben.
- Can you share the procurement timeline and the name of the procurement lead? (Jordan/Procurement email ok) — owner: Samira.
- Security questionnaire: I’ve attached our SLA draft; if you can send your security questionnaire, we’ll map evidence to controls — owner: Karthik.
- Proposed pilot window: Jan 10 — Feb 10 (2 weeks pilot, 3 week ramp to full committed baseline). If that works, we’ll prepare the Pilot Agreement / DocuSign.

Attachments: helixa-compute-worksheet.xlsx, sla-draft-helixa-v1.docx

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
---

From: Samira Khan <samira@helixa.ai>

Subject: Re: Ops constraints, ramp timeline, and tenant segmentation plan - follow-up (Helixa)

Tessa —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Procurement lead: attaching initial contact (procurement@helixa.ai). We’re targeting an internal finance review week of Jan 4 and would ideally kick the pilot the following week.
- Minimum commit: we typically look for a 3–6 month runway. For the pilot we can sign a 1 month pilot with an option to convert. Can you call out a recommended minimum SKU (e.g., 8x A10-equivalent GPUs or similar)?
- Security: attaching our questionnaire (helixa-security-questions.xlsx). Please map your controls to the items labeled PHI and encryption at rest.

Quick note: demo peaks are often tied to concurrent users during clinical Q&A sessions — expect 10–15 short bursts of high concurrency rather than sustained load. That influences burst policy and cache TTLs.

Thanks — I’ll loop procurement once we have the worksheet and a high-level SOW.

Samira Khan
Head of Platform Engineering
Helixa Therapeutics

Subject: Re: Ops constraints, ramp timeline, and tenant segmentation plan - follow-up (Helixa)

Samira / Jordan —

Thanks for the quick reply and the questionnaire. High level responses and concrete proposal below so procurement has a clear starting point.

Sizing & commit recommendation
- Pilot: 2 dedicated slots (each slot = 4x A10-equivalent GPUs) for Jan 10 – Feb 10 to validate latency + isolation.
- Baseline committed reservation: 4 dedicated slots (16 GPUs total) to meet steady throughput and isolation needs.
- Burst: policy-driven access to a shared pool that can add up to an additional 8 GPUs for short periods; throttles and auto-fallback to a quantized variant of the model to protect latency SLOs.

SLA & security mapping
- Availability: Redwood committed SLA for the dedicated pool = 99.95% monthly.
- Auditing: per-tenant request logs, KMS‑backed key separation, and 90+ day retention (we’ll map fields to Helixa questionnaire — Ben will own the mapping).

Cost framing (very rough)
- Pilot (1 month): estimate attached in the worksheet (row "pilot-2slot") — this is intentionally conservative to cover peak bursts.
- Committed baseline: monthly committed price delivered in the worksheet; we’ll model a 6–12 month term for better economics.

Action items & owners
- Ben: finalize and upload the worksheet with pilot & baseline rows by tomorrow EOD.
- Tessa: prepare a short Pilot SOW + DocuSign template for procurement to review.
- Samira/Jordan: confirm procurement lead and preferred signatory, and confirm the Jan 10 pilot start (or propose alternatives by Dec 22).

If procurement would like to see a hands-on demo of the burst behavior and tracing for a sample request flow, we can schedule a short ops session (30–45m) during week of Jan 3.
